Walking Decisions

These decisions do not require Codex, the repository, or a computer. They are good tasks for walks, voice notes, or ChatGPT discussions.

The purpose is to finish judgment-heavy thinking before sitting down to execute.

1. Website Purpose

Decide what the website is primarily for.

Possible goals:

  • Accurate public representation of who I am now
  • Personal hub / canonical identity
  • Credibility
  • Networking
  • Recruiting / attracting collaborators
  • Audience building
  • Personal documentation
  • Showing accomplishments
  • Showing current projects
  • Showing personality / making the site fun

Decision:

  • Choose the top 1-3 primary goals
  • Decide what the website should not optimize for

This decision should guide Home, About, navigation, design, and what gets removed.

2. Public Identity

  • Decide canonical public name; decision: Goku
    • Goku
    • Goktug Yilmaz
    • Goku (Goktug Yilmaz)
    • another hybrid
  • Decide final identity line; decision: Engineer, entrepreneur, gamer, biohacker
    • Entrepreneur
    • Engineer
    • Gamer
    • Biohacker
    • Digital Nomad
    • other
  • Decide whether “Investor” belongs in the identity at all; decision: no, keep it in the dedicated Investing section
  • Decide whether “homeless” is:
    • not used
    • an Easter egg/joke
    • a visible descriptor
  • Decide how professional vs playful the public identity should feel

3. Goku Brand / Domain Strategy

  • Decide whether Goku is the permanent public brand
  • Consider Dragon Ball / Son Goku confusion
  • Consider searchability and discoverability
  • Decide whether having a Goku-domain is important
  • Decide whether goktug.io remains canonical or becomes a redirect
  • Decide whether old identity should remain visible for search/history

No domain purchase or migration is needed during the walk. This is only the naming/brand decision.

4. Website Information Architecture

Decide the top-level structure before redesigning pages.

Possible top-level pages:

  • Home
  • About
  • Now
  • Projects
  • Gaming
  • Health / Biohacking
  • Travel
  • Writing
  • Books
  • Quotes
  • Archive

Decide:

  • Which deserve top-level navigation
  • Which should be sections inside About
  • Which should be archived
  • Which should disappear
  • Whether “Now” deserves its own page or a Home section
  • Whether Projects deserves its own page

5. Content Hierarchy

  • Decide what should appear above the fold on Home
  • Decide the 3-5 most important things a stranger should know
  • Decide which accomplishments are still worth showing
  • Decide what historical content should be demoted to archive
  • Decide what should be removed entirely
  • Decide how much Colonist should dominate the site

6. Gamification Philosophy

  • Decide how much of the site should feel game-like
  • Decide what must remain clean/minimal
  • Decide whether game UI is:
    • subtle
    • medium
    • strong on selected pages only
  • Decide which concepts are worth gamifying:
    • achievements
    • ranks
    • quests
    • stats
    • progress bars
    • rarity tiers
    • unlocks
    • world exploration
  • Decide what should never be gamified

Design principle to preserve unless deliberately changed:

The website should remain a clean personal website. Game UI appears where progression, stats, achievements, or exploration naturally exist.

7. Health / Biohacking Public Content

  • Decide final page name:
    • Health
    • Fitness
    • Biohacking
    • Health & Performance
  • Decide which metrics are public
  • Decide which goals are public
  • Decide whether body composition numbers are public
  • Decide whether sleep/HRV data is public
  • Decide whether strength PRs are public
  • Decide whether current experiments/protocols are public
  • Decide whether this page is a snapshot or continuously updated character sheet

8. Travel / Privacy

  • Decide whether “Digital Nomad” alone is enough for the main identity; decision: yes, use it as the public location descriptor
  • Decide whether current city is public
  • Decide whether current region is public
  • Decide whether travel history is public
  • Decide how precise dates should be
  • Decide whether Nomad List should be linked; decision: link the public Nomads profile as the Digital Nomad location descriptor
  • Decide whether public travel information should live entirely on goktug.io instead
  • Decide what location information should never be public

9. External Profiles

  • Decide whether LinkedIn is worth recreating
  • Decide which profiles are worth linking publicly
  • Decide whether GitHub, Stack Overflow, Medium, HackerNoon, Nomad List, etc. still add value
  • Decide whether any public profile exposes more personal information than it is worth
  • Decide whether goktug.io should become the canonical profile instead of depending on social platforms

10. Investments

Decision (August 10, 2026): Keep a concise Investing section focused on approach, learning, and participation rather than holdings, returns, or portfolio performance. Investment is a meaningful secondary practice, not part of the primary public identity line.

  • Decide whether investing is meaningful enough to represent publicly; decision: yes, as a concise section
  • Decide whether secondary/crowdfunding/private-market investments are worth listing
  • Decide whether an investment section would communicate substance or just signaling; decision: explain the strategy without listing holdings, returns, or exits
  • Define the current strategy: primarily invest through trusted early-stage-focused fund managers and angels; invest directly only when close to the product, people, mission, or problem

11. Quotes Page

  • Keep
  • Update
  • Redesign
  • Archive
  • Remove

If kept:

  • Decide whether quotes still represent current values
  • Decide whether personal commentary/context should be added

12. Visual / Media Direction

  • Decide whether to add more:
    • photos
    • travel imagery
    • project screenshots
    • game artwork
    • company/product visuals
  • Decide whether the site should remain mostly text-based
  • Decide whether personal photos are worth the privacy/exposure tradeoff

13. Graduation Criteria

This website is a prerequisite project, not an endless redesign.

Before moving to the Anime Tierlist project, decide whether I need to be comfortable with:

  • local development
  • Git/GitHub
  • Codex execution
  • reviewing diffs
  • debugging simple failures
  • deploying
  • small multi-file changes
  • iterative UI work
  • agent-led implementation with human judgment

Project sequence:

Personal Website → Anime Tierlist UI → Personal OS V0 → Personal OS V1+ → Company OS

The website project is complete when the site is good enough and the learning goals are achieved.

14. Audience & First Impression

The website will be intentionally sent to people, so it must work as a strong introduction rather than only a personal archive.

Target Audience

  • Decide the primary audiences: founders, engineers, collaborators, hires, investors/business contacts, friends/social contacts, random visitors
  • Rank the top 1-3 audiences
  • Decide whether the site should optimize for everyone or intentionally prioritize a few groups

15-Second Test

A visitor should quickly understand:

  • Who is Goku?
  • What does he do?
  • What has he accomplished?
  • What makes him unusual?
  • Define the exact 15-second impression I want

60-Second Test

A visitor should understand:

  • What has he built?
  • What is he obsessed with now?
  • What connects gaming, engineering, entrepreneurship, biohacking, nomadism, and AI?
  • Why might I want to know, follow, work with, or talk to him?
  • Define the exact 60-second impression I want

15. Personal Narrative / Life Thread

The site should not only be a database of accomplishments.

Possible story:

Gamer who optimized games → learned programming through games and automation → built software/products → became a founder → built Colonist → designed life around autonomy and nomadism → started optimizing health/body/life → now builds AI systems to optimize life and work.

  • Decide whether this is the correct narrative
  • Rewrite it in my own words
  • Decide which transitions/events are essential
  • Decide where this narrative belongs: Home, About, timeline, or separate story section
  • Preserve old-site material that makes the story authentic

16. Proof & Credibility Standard

Rule to consider:

Extraordinary claim → evidence or careful wording.

  • Decide which accomplishments need proof
  • Decide which numbers need dates/context
  • Decide when links, screenshots, videos, rankings, GitHub, press, or archived evidence improve credibility
  • Decide when a claim should be softened because evidence is unavailable
  • Avoid unsupported absolute language where precise wording is stronger

17. Voice / Bragging / Professionalism

  • Decide how boastful, playful, and professional the site should be
  • Decide whether first-person casual language remains part of the voice
  • Decide where humor belongs
  • Preserve intentional weirdness/personality
  • Remove accidental weirdness caused by stale, exaggerated, or contextless writing

Principle:

Do not sterilize the site into LinkedIn 2.0. Keep the unusual parts that genuinely explain who I am.

18. Reputation / Public Content Audit

Every public page should be judged not only for accuracy, but for the impression it creates without context.

  • Decide whether publication implies endorsement
  • Review jokes, old opinions, old claims, and outdated identity statements
  • Review quotes from controversial people
  • Review exaggerated/absolute language
  • Review content that worked as a personal archive but may be poor as something intentionally sent to others
  • Decide what historical content should move to Archive

Quotes-specific decision

  • Replace with a smaller curated “Ideas I Like” collection
  • Add commentary/context to selected quotes
  • Keep the full historical collection only in Archive
  • Remove quotes that no longer represent anything useful
  • Clearly distinguish “interesting quote I saved” from “idea I endorse”

19. Values / Worldview

Core values: Freedom · Mastery · Achievement · Vitality · Enjoyment

Decision (August 10, 2026): Treat these values as private context and an editorial compass, not as a standalone values section on the public website. Let visitors infer them from concrete work, choices, stories, and personality:

  • Freedom: autonomy, entrepreneurship, ownership, and nomadism
  • Mastery: engineering, gaming, learning, and deliberate practice
  • Achievement: verified accomplishments and meaningful progress
  • Vitality: health, fitness, energy, and biohacking

  • Enjoyment: games, humor, relationships, personality, and designing an enjoyable life

  • Decide whether “My Goal in Life” still represents me
  • Decide whether Singleplayer / Multiplayer framing should remain
  • Decide whether current core values belong on the site; decision: related evidence belongs, not a generic values list
  • Decide whether values should be explicit or emerge through the story; decision: emerge through the story
  • Update rather than remove distinctive worldview content if it still fits

20. Current Obsessions

Possible areas:

  • Colonist
  • Personal OS / AI Brain
  • AI learning / building
  • health / biohacking
  • physique / performance
  • gaming
  • travel / digital nomadism

Decide:

  • Which 2-4 belong on Home
  • Which belong only on deeper pages
  • How frequently they should be updated

21. Social Proof

  • Decide which numbers strengthen credibility
  • Decide which accomplishments deserve prominence
  • Decide whether company/player/revenue/open-source/game statistics should be shown
  • Add dates/context to historical metrics
  • Prefer meaningful proof over many weak vanity metrics

22. Visitor Action / Contact

Decide what, if anything, I want visitors to do:

  • contact me
  • play Colonist
  • follow my current work
  • read writing
  • view GitHub/projects
  • collaborate
  • hire/work with me
  • nothing; the site is primarily an identity/reference page

If contact is enabled:

  • Decide what contact method to expose
  • Decide what kinds of messages/opportunities I want
  • Decide what I do not want to invite
  • Write boundaries if useful

23. Update / Freshness Strategy

Classify content as:

  • Evergreen
  • Periodic
  • Current
  • Automatic/structured

Decide:

  • Which sections must stay current
  • How often each should be reviewed
  • Whether “Last updated” should exist
  • Whether stale current-content should disappear automatically
  • Which data could later be maintained by Personal OS / AI agents
